verdict.rationale: Yubico's own docs confirm NFC-enabled YubiKeys exist and work with phones. YubiKit Android supports NFC keys and includes a FIDO2/WebAuthn client with WebView integration, and YubiKit iOS reads OTPs from NFC keys on NFC-enabled iOS devices. However, this support is shown only through app SDKs; nothing documents tap-to-authenticate in mobile browsers like Safari or Chrome, or FIDO2/passkey over NFC on iOS. Missing for 10: documented NFC passkey/WebAuthn login in mobile browsers, iOS FIDO2-over-NFC evidence, hands-on or independent corroboration of NFC phone use.

support.subject: As a power user, I can tap the key on my phone over NFC to authenticate in mobile browsers and apps

citations.quote: Both USB and NFC-enabled YubiKeys are supported.
The library supports NFC-enabled YubiKeys and provides the APIs to request an OTP (Yubico OTP or HOTP) from the NFC YubiKeys using a NFC-enabled iOS device.
provides a high-level FIDO2/WebAuthn client with built-in UI components, WebView integration, and customizable theming
